items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: I worked with Henry after, after I left Pete.

ctx.x: And Henry asked him, he said, what'd you fire me for? He said, we don't need you no more. We're doing business. We don't need a man anymore. Uh-huh. So, they, then he let him go. And, uh, Joe never would have told me that, but, uh, Henry did tell me that, because I was, I worked with Henry after, after I left Pete. And I was with Henry with, who was booking most of the Lou Wopps jobs. And, uh, in fact, we had quite a, with Rene, he didn't want, he didn't want Henry to use me. items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: What happened to a lot of musicians, I mean I know, Louis Macenta, Henry Newfield, and several guys, I can't think of their names

ctx.x: You'd hit a certain note on the Wagner phone... And everything would explode. You know the old glass... Vibrations. The Wagner phone was gonna do it. Without a doubt... He finally, after he gave up music... He became a professor down at one of the high schools down there. The one that was... I think it was Nichols. ! Where they had the Confederate flag.
